text: Setting clear goals is essential for any project’s success. A useful method is to follow the SMART criteria: goals should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying “improve the website,” a SMART goal would be “increase customer sign-ups by 15% within three months.” Once your main goal is set, break it into smaller milestones. These are checkpoints that help you track progress and stay motivated. Each milestone should lead to a clear deliverable, such as a report or a prototype. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment from the start. This means talking to everyone involved to confirm that the objectives meet their expectations. When all parties share the same vision, the project moves forward much more smoothly.
